name: batch:SubmitJob
description: A principal with only batch:SubmitJob can escalate privileges by submitting a job to an existing Batch job queue using a pre-existing job definition that already has an admin jobRoleArn. The ContainerOverrides.Command field allows the submitter to replace the container's default command with any arbitrary command — including iam:AttachUserPolicy — which executes using the job definition's admin role credentials. No iam:PassRole or batch:RegisterJobDefinition is required because the privileged role was already assigned to the existing job definition.
author: Seth Art

required.description: Must be able to submit to the target job queue

additional.description: Helpful for discovering job definitions with privileged jobRoleArns
Helpful for discovering available job queues
Useful for polling job execution status
Helpful for understanding compute environment configuration

admin: An existing Batch job definition must already have an admin IAM role set as the jobRoleArn
An existing Batch job queue must be available to submit jobs to
lateral: An existing Batch job definition must have an elevated IAM role set as the jobRoleArn
An existing Batch job queue must be available

references.title: Messing Around With AWS Batch For Privilege Escalations - Doyensec
How AWS Batch works with IAM

options.name: JOB_DEFINITION
options.description: Name or ARN of the existing Batch job definition with privileged jobRoleArn

options.name: JOB_QUEUE
options.description: Name or ARN of the Batch job queue to submit the job to

options.name: PAYLOAD
options.description: Payload type to execute inside the Batch job container (backdoor/attach-policy, exfil/https)

options.name: CONTAINER_RUNTIME
options.description: Container entrypoint type: 'aws-cli' (default, container entrypoint is 'aws' — e.g. amazon/aws-cli:latest) or 'generic' (container has sh + aws CLI — e.g. Ubuntu, Debian). exfil/https requires 'generic'.

options.name: TARGET_PRINCIPAL
options.description: IAM username or role name to attach AdministratorAccess to (auto-resolved from caller identity if not set)

options.name: REGION
options.description: AWS region for Batch and IAM operations

options.name: CLEANUP
options.description: Detach AdministratorAccess from TARGET_PRINCIPAL after execution. Requires iam:DetachUserPolicy or iam:DetachRolePolicy.

payloads.name: backdoor/attach-policy
payloads.description: Attach AdministratorAccess (or any managed policy) to an IAM user or role via Batch job container command

payloads.name: backdoor/create-access-key
payloads.description: Create programmatic access keys for an IAM user via Batch job container command

payloads.name: backdoor/create-role
payloads.description: Create an IAM role with AdministratorAccess and a custom trust policy via Batch job (requires CONTAINER_RUNTIME=generic)

payloads.name: backdoor/create-user
payloads.description: Create an IAM user with AdministratorAccess and optional console/programmatic access via Batch job (requires CONTAINER_RUNTIME=generic)

payloads.name: backdoor/update-role-trust
payloads.description: Append a trust policy statement to an existing IAM role via Batch job (requires CONTAINER_RUNTIME=generic with jq)

payloads.name: exfil/https
payloads.description: Exfiltrate Batch task role credentials to an attacker HTTPS endpoint; detects curl/wget/python at runtime (requires CONTAINER_RUNTIME=generic)
